# RunToMax

> RunToMax is a running app for iPhone and Apple Watch. It records runs on the Apple Watch and coaches from the runs already in Apple Health: a plain-language verdict after every run, a threshold pace estimated from the last 90 days, and race-date training plans that propose changes the runner approves. For runners aged 18 and older. English and French.

## Facts (checked against App Store version 1.2.3, 2026-09-22)

- Requirements: iPhone with iOS 17 or later; Apple Watch with watchOS 10 or later (Series 4 and newer, SE, Ultra). Recording requires the Apple Watch; no phone needed on the run.
- Other watches (Garmin, Coros, Polar, Suunto): runs synced to Apple Health can be read, with basic data only (distance, time, heart rate). Direct sync is planned, not available.
- Strava: sync is built and in limited testing; not in the App Store version. Runs are written to Apple Health and can be exported as FIT files.
- Price (US): RunToMax Pro, $29.99/year with a 14-day free trial or $5.99/month with a 7-day trial, billed by Apple. One subscription unlocks the whole app. No free tier; recorded runs stay in Apple Health regardless.
- Cloud coaching is opt-in and produces only the longer written coach notes; everything else (profile, paces, run classification, verdict, plans, scores, readiness, heat adjustment) runs on the iPhone.
- Data: no account, no cloud copy of training history, no ads, no data sale.
- Developer: Hidai Bar-Mor, independent developer.

## Accuracy summary

- Distance uses Apple's workout distance engine. Against a Garmin on the other wrist: within about 1% on steady runs; 1–3% short on interval and stop-heavy runs, mostly from pause handling. More than 35 paired runs since May 2026; a 17-run scored corpus gates any change to the distance code.
- Cadence matches the Garmin (median 180 vs 181 spm). Elevation from the barometer with GPS drift correction, about 9 m per run. Ground contact time from the wrist is not used for form guidance.
